subject: Email ConvertToHtml cleanup hardening — beyond GC.Collect
sprint26_fix: Wrapped FolderOutputHandler in inner scope block + GC.Collect() x2 + GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers()

sprint27_hardening_assessment.workaround_determinism: NON_DETERMINISTIC — GC.Collect() forces collection but finalizer execution is not guaranteed to be immediate on all CLR configurations
sprint27_hardening_assessment.workaround_stability: STABLE_IN_PRACTICE — 5/5 ALL_PASS confirmed in Sprint 27 run

alternatives_evaluated.description: Retry File.ReadAllText with 100ms sleep up to 5 times if IOException
alternatives_evaluated.tradeoff: More robust than GC.Collect but adds retry complexity
alternatives_evaluated.verdict: OPTIONAL_IMPROVEMENT — current approach works in practice

alternatives_evaluated.description: Use a fresh unique output directory for each test run so lock contention never occurs
Open output file with FileShare.ReadWrite after conversion
alternatives_evaluated.tradeoff: Does not help — FolderOutputHandler uses exclusive write lock with no sharing flag

alternatives_evaluated.description: FolderOutputHandler does not implement IDisposable or expose a completion event

sprint27_hardening_assessment.hardening_recommendation: Current GC.Collect() pattern is sufficient for test harness. For production template_first code, document that FolderOutputHandler output directory should not be read in the same synchronous scope without GC flush or retry.
sprint27_hardening_assessment.template_first_note: The generated example code should NOT read from the FolderOutputHandler output directory in the same execution flow. The example's validation uses result.ResultCollection, not a post-hoc file read — so the file lock issue does not affect the generated example, only the harness.

verdict: EMAIL_CONVERTTOHTML_HARDENING_ASSESSED — GC.Collect workaround stable (5/5 ALL_PASS Sprint 27). Alternatives evaluated: retry-with-backoff optional improvement, unique-dir already applied, FileShare/IDisposable blocked by library.
